first_party_call_path.integrated_client_server: IntegratedServer extends MinecraftServer for each inspected version. It has no constant-pool reference to ServerTextFilter or PlayerSafetyServiceTextFilter. MinecraftServer.createTextFilterForPlayer returns the TextFilter.DUMMY singleton; vanilla integrated-server chat therefore does not enter the server moderation filter.
first_party_call_path.dedicated_server: DedicatedServer constructor calls ServerTextFilter.createFromConfig(DedicatedServerProperties). ServerTextFilter returns null for a blank config; configured version 0 creates LegacyTextFilter and version 1 creates PlayerSafetyServiceTextFilter. DedicatedServerProperties defaults text-filtering-config to empty and text-filtering-version to 0. The PlayerSafety filter obtains a token from MSAL using HTTPS authority login.microsoftonline.com/{tenantId}/, adds a Bearer authorization header to the configured moderation endpoint request, serializes player chat and parses moderation API responses using Gson. MSAL separately parses identity discovery/token JSON with Jackson JsonHelper.
first_party_call_path.third_party_library_reflection: Jackson databind uses reflection internally to construct the explicit DTO class passed to readValue(String, Class). Both exact MSAL versions were scanned for reflection classloader APIs, default typing/PTV APIs, async parser creation, DataInput parser references, and Jackson identity/type annotations. No API-trigger references were found for the six corresponding advisory-specific preconditions. This does not inspect all runtime code or arbitrary reflective calls outside MSAL.
first_party_call_path.attacker_input_boundary: Network game chat is serialized to the configured moderation service with Gson and its response is parsed with Gson. The Jackson parser input on the first-party path is MSAL identity discovery/token data from HTTPS Microsoft identity endpoints. The report does not establish remote attacker control of those responses, custom trust stores, tenant-controlled claims, or custom launcher changes.

jackson_2_13_4_tests.observed: All generated inputs parsed without StackOverflowError in the bounded test runs.

isolated_dynamic_probe.interpretation: The 2.13.4 tests did not reproduce the upstream StackOverflowError for these JSON shapes up to the tested depths. The 2.15.0 probe demonstrates the fixed default nesting guard. Neither observation establishes process-wide safety or compatibility of a game-library override.

first_party_call_path.log4j_core_callers: The exact runtime manifest also supplies Log4j Core 2.22.1 for 1.21.2–1.21.3 and 2.24.1 for 1.21.4–1.21.10. Both contain Jackson JSON configuration/parser/layout classes. JsonConfiguration reads a selected JSON configuration stream with ObjectMapper.readTree; JsonLogEventParser exposes public parseFrom methods that use a typed ObjectReader for Log4jLogEvent. Exact Mojang default launcher metadata points to client-1.21.2.xml (same SHA-1/size for all nine); that file selects LegacyXMLLayout and PatternLayout only. No JSON/YAML layout, public event parser call, or built-in SocketServer listener is selected by that default. Custom launcher config and external mod code could reach these APIs; no supported launcher trace or third-party mod inventory is available.

limitations: No exact supported production launcher command lines/classpaths were captured for these source groups.
No arbitrary third-party mod set, custom launcher, Java agent, or reflective runtime mutation was inventoried.
The tested default integrated-server path is not a substitute for observing every modded process.
The isolated nesting probe did not reproduce the upstream DoS within tested depths and does not clear that advisory.
No game-managed dependency upgrade or mod-controlled fix was applied; advisory counts remain unchanged.

disassembly_observations: JsonConfiguration constructs a default ObjectMapper and calls readTree(InputStream) for a selected JSON Log4j configuration file.
JsonLogEventParser has a public constructor and public parseFrom(String), parseFrom(byte[]), and parseFrom(byte[], offset, length) methods.
AbstractJacksonLogEventParser creates an ObjectReader for the concrete Log4jLogEvent class and calls ObjectReader.readValue(String or byte[]).
JacksonFactory builds ObjectWriter serialization paths for JSON/XML/YAML layouts.

Within the exact Log4j Core JAR, no class references JsonLogEventParser except its own class; XmlLogEventParser and YamlLogEventParser reference their corresponding parser base. No built-in SocketServer/TcpSocketServer/InputStreamLogEventBridge classes are present.
log4j_core_runtime_analysis.reachability: Potential public third-party/mod caller exists, and a custom local JSON logging configuration is parsed with Jackson. Mojang’s default external XML config does not select these routes; a remote attacker-controlled feed into JsonLogEventParser was not found in Log4j Core itself.
